label: Overheat in the hard data, markets pricing a turn toward Slowdown
why: Official data shows growth rising (Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%, ISM manufacturing 55.5, services 54.5, claims 189k) and inflation rising (Oct PCE 3.8% y/y, core 3.3%). Markets disagree: oil -18% in 1m, 10y breakeven down 22bp to 2.12%, copper -18%, HY spreads widest of 2026 at 3.72%, cyclicals/defensives -10% over 3m, VIX 28. Markets are the early warning, hard data the confirmation (CLAUDE.md 4.2), so the working read is late Overheat with a live Slowdown transition risk.

overlays.rates: Fed hiking bias (Oct 28 hold 10-2, two dissents for a hike; Dec 8-9 hike is base case) while long yields fall: 2y 4.61%, 10y 4.85%, 30y 5.24% (2026-11-25). Curve positive ~24bp.
overlays.dollar: Up: DXY 103.67, +4.8% over 3m. Tightening for foreign earners and emerging markets.
overlays.credit: Widening: HY OAS 3.72%, +105bp since August, widest of 2026.
overlays.liquidity: Tightening: Fed hiking, dollar up, risk-off (VIX 35.9 peak on 11-20).

disagreements.who_might_be_wrong: ISM is a survey and may lag a turn; copper and credit lead
markets read the oil shock as passing; Fed reads it as sticky

disagreements.hard_data: Fed leaning to a December hike
disagreements.who_might_be_wrong: a hike into a slowdown is the classic policy error; or the long end is pricing growth damage

disagreements.market: HY spreads widest of 2026, cyclicals/defensives -10%, SPY -6.9% 1m
disagreements.who_might_be_wrong: GDP is backward-looking; credit is forward-looking

disagreements.hard_data: nominal retail sales inflated by fuel
disagreements.who_might_be_wrong: real consumer spending was flat in October: the consumer is weaker than nominal data shows
